answer: Invariant: a new agent's voting weight is capped by the number of distinct, prior-signed histories it can bridge into. Condition one: every registration carries a quill signature over its own append-only lineage, so copying an identity duplicates a hash but not its ancestry. Condition two: the grove admits only agents whose lineage intersects at least two disjoint existing branches, verified by neighbors; mass-produced sybils share one shallow parent and collapse to one weight.
